newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian market makers fall as oil shares rise.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian market makers fall as oil shares rise.

text.p: Shares of conglomerate John Holt led the pack as the slide of blue chips continued on the Nigerian stock market on Monday, traders said.
The all-share index had not been updated as at 1800 GMT. It closed 6617.86 last Friday.
John Holt plunged by the maximum five percent, down 55 kobo, to 10.43 naira as investors resumed selling large volumes.
Traders said a bearish trend seemed to have crept in early ahead of the Christmas season due to economic difficulties confronting most firms.
"There is no money in the economy, a situation which forces investors to divest from stocks considered to have gained appreciably during the year," one trader said.
Another highly capitalised conglomerate UAC fell 10 kobo to 9.90 naira for the same reason.
Big brewers, Nigerian Breweries and Guinness, among the hardest hit by the trend, fell again on Monday by 20 kobo and 10 kobo, respectively, to 11.30 naira and 7.30 naira.

Ashaka Cement, which enjoyed an impressive run until last Friday, fell 20 kobo on Monday to 18.90 naira. But sectoral leader West African Portland Cement was up 10 kobo at 35.60 naira, while upward-moving Benue Cement rose 20 kobo to 7.52 naira.

Food shares also closed down as Flour Mills dropped 20 kobo at 11.00, while Cadbury shed five kobo to 26.40 naira. But Nestle Foods, still enjoying a favourable perception after an improved six-month result rose 20 kobo to 35.80 naira.
The strongest gains were recorded in the oil marketing sector where investors seem to be increasing their stakes.
Three key oil stocks closed 40 kobo up. National Oil was 36.20 naira, Total ended at 48.40 naira and Unipetrol shot to 43.20 naira.
African Petroleum went 20 kobo up to 34.70 naira, but Agip, Texaco and Mobil were unchanged at 15.20 naira and 27.40 naira and 41.00 naira, respectively.
The sector is rising on the expectation it will give investors good returns, dealers said.
Insurance and packaging shares also made modest gains because of their relatively cheap prices.
AIICO Insurance went up by 15 kobo to 7.50 naira while UNIC added five kobo to 3.85 naira.
Renewed demand for Delta Glass boosted its shares by five kobo to 6.15 naira while Van Leer rose six kobo to 12.36 naira.
